scope: Expected authorization outcomes only; no SQL, JWT validation, RLS engine, or API execution is supplied by this fixture.
identity_mapping: Symbolic IDs must be mapped to real synthetic Auth users and tenant IDs in the learner's isolated project. Never generate a user JWT by trusting these strings.
rules: Only an active membership grants access. Read all documents in the member's own tenant.
A member may insert a document owned by themselves in their own tenant.
A member may update only the title of their own document.
An admin may update titles or delete documents within their own tenant, never another tenant.
tenant_id and owner_id are immutable through this application API, including for tenant admins.
Membership changes come from trusted server state, not editable user_metadata or request fields.
Every write case starts from the original fixture; denied writes leave all rows unchanged.
Privileged maintenance is a separate server-only path and is not a tenant-admin session.
assertion_contract: Compare visible payload/IDs and independently inspected post-state, not HTTP status alone.
An unauthorized read may be filtered to zero rows or rejected earlier by grants; it must not expose another tenant's payload.
An unauthorized update/delete may affect zero rows without an HTTP error; assert that no forbidden row changed.
Validate allowed new state values too, not only changed row IDs; denied writes require byte-equivalent protected state.
R06/W12 require server-side membership revocation to take effect despite a stale user token. A claim-only design fails this chosen business contract.
Run with actual user sessions. Owner/superuser/BYPASSRLS SQL tests do not prove client isolation.
Actual API, view, RPC, Storage, and Realtime tests remain separate implementation tasks.
